Resolves #21903
Related: #21942

The featured GitHub Issues Grid was ready to photograph in both themes. Five lazy avatars began at x=943, four pixels beyond the grid’s overflow edge. Their layout boxes overlapped the 960 × 540 viewport, but Chromium gave each a 0 × 0 intersection. The camera waited 15 seconds for images the browser never requested.

The camera now asks Chromium how much of each unready image or video is visible after ancestor clipping, then intersects that with the requested screenshot region. A single visible pixel keeps the capture waiting. The same check applies to gallery cards and Workbench tile crops.

Evidence: L3 (two ordinary Issues Grid launches per palette and browser controls for clipped, visible and partially visible media) → L3 required.

## AC Evidence

| Reopened AC-2 | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Recipe-less capture of a real example | With only the legacy `grid-issues` recipe omitted in a temporary producer, the ordinary camera wrote dark and light 1280 × 720 JPEGs without a click or scroll. Both files reproduced byte-for-byte on the second launch. The head leaves the tracked recipe and catalog untouched. |
| Clipped media | The component test failed on the previous predicate when an image touched the scroller edge. It passes with the corrected predicate. Native intersection can report edge contact with zero area, which contributes no painted pixel. |
| Visible broken and partial media | A broken image with one pixel inside the scroller or the capture region still times out. A decoded image at the same position passes. A partially visible video with an unready source also times out. |

| Dark opening | Light opening |

Frame critique: in both palettes the fixed State column hides most of the Author column at 960 CSS pixels. The edge of its header is visible, and the separated Open and Closed states remain legible. The covers preserve this actual layout along with the wrapped titles and search control.

### `@neo-opus-vega` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-23T05:12:21Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — one readiness predicate in the cover camera plus its spec. The new `paintReady` export has one consumer, its spec; no engine, runtime or consumed contract changes.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The camera now counts media as visible only where Chromium's clipped intersection (`IntersectionObserver`, implicit root) puts a pixel inside the capture, which is the clipping the browser's own lazy loader sees. Every clip lies inside the viewport (`captureRegion` refuses one that doesn't), so bounding the intersection by the viewport loses no part of a capture. The diff touches no site beyond the predicate, its JSDoc and the export its spec needs. Verified on `d8afed2d0e`:
- The spec passes 4/4. With the merged predicate swapped into the same poll wrapper, both new arms time out: red on `dev`, green on the head.
- The real record, with the `grid-issues` recipe removed in a scratch worktree: the 960×540 landing writes dark and light 1280×720 covers, byte-identical across two runs (`00aedd876e47`, `8192befa9c22`). Under the merged predicate both themes time out.
- What I looked for and did not find: unloaded media the new predicate lets into the frame. Each row of the cover shows a sliver at the Area column's edge, but it is the `issues-chip` border. The author avatars (x 943–967) report a 0×0 intersection behind the locked State column.

**Findings:**
- [ ] Optional, no re-review needed: the old summary said why the constant is `1800` (Chromium's ~1.5 s initial `<video controls>` overlay). The new summary drops that, so `captureExamples.mjs:593` now reads as a magic number. If you push again, a trailing comment there restores it.
